$0.20 per install, even if your app is free, is insane. Unreal and Godot are serious competitors now. I dont see how Unity thinks this will work.

For developers the per-install fee is an additional unwelcome cost... For gamers, this seem to indicate that all games developed with Unity phone home back to Unity HQ... with information about my machine.
I switched to unreal several years ago because Unity had written hundreds of gigabytes of log files complaining that it could not phone home and filled up my hard drive
I used XNA, then MS killed it for no reason, then I switched to Unity, been using it since 2012, today I'm learning Godot... Imo Godot is the new indie engine. it has the same feel as XNA and Unity.
Unity forced my last company into the more expensive license unilaterally and with no discussion. They doubled our costs just because they can.
The extravagant cost of a Unity seat meant we couldn't afford to give anyone except the Unity devs a license... we couldn't set up a build server in our CI system. It was an absolute nightmare.

VLC-Unity plugin is fully open source... We've had discussions for years with Apple AppStore, Google Play store, and Windows Stores... but Unity was a headache an order of magnitude bigger: no answers, 3 different answers contradicting each other, and plain bad faith. (VideoLAN President)
Unity basically told us we were not welcome back to their Store, ever. Even if we were to remove all LGPL code from the Unity package.
I've been watching a few gamedev streamers port their games to Godot and it's clear that it's not there yet in terms of feature parity... some major things (profiling?) are miles off still.

What Unity offers is a solid way to build cross platform and target iOS. They're able to offer that because they have the resources to keep up with iOS. Open-source alternatives understandably struggle to keep on the iOS treadmill.

Unity's mishandling of the Runtime Fee policy announcement has caused permanent damage to their reputation... Every single one that uses Unity today is planning to switch engines for their future games.

Unity forced my last company into the more expensive license unilaterally and with no discussion. They doubled our costs just because they can. At this point, we should all treat Unity like we do Broadcom—utterly toxic.

The extravagant cost of a Unity seat meant we couldn't afford to give anyone except the Unity devs a license... For the same reason, we couldn't set up a build server in our CI system. It was an absolute nightmare.

This shows once again that Unity is an unreliable option for new projects. The worst part is not the 4% fee, but the bluntness with which Unity has administered these changes—terms can change at any moment.
